title: The new model came out
scenario: Lantern Studio re-runs its Fernhill Candles test suite on a new image model. You judge the results and the upkeep of the suite, using the exhibit. The jobs, results and counts are made up for this case. The dates are from OpenAI's deprecations page.
exhibit:
SUITE (made up for this case)
  Regression jobs: 25. Last quarter, the current model passed 25 of 25.
  Capability jobs: 8. Last quarter, the current model passed 3 of 8.

NEW MODEL RUN (made up)
  Regression: 23 of 25 passed. Failed: R-07 (logo), R-19 (label text).
  Capability: 6 of 8 passed.
  All jobs together: 29 of 33 passed (88%).

CLIENT COMPLAINT (made up)
  A wrap-around jar label came out with the logo upside down.
  No job in the suite covers a wrap-around label.

REPEAT RUN (made up)
  Job R-12, logo line: right in 9 of 10 runs.
  A client brief asks for a set of 3 images, all with the logo right.

SUITE HISTORY (made up)
  The 25 regression jobs have scored 25 of 25 for six months.

WHERE THE SUITE LIVES (made up)
  The rubric, the jobs and the past scores are stored only in the
  OpenAI Evals platform.
  Date: 2026-10-07.
  Deprecations page: existing evals become read-only on Oct 31, 2026;
  the Evals dashboard and API are scheduled to shut down on Nov 30, 2026.

questions.prompt: How should the studio read the new model's run?

options.text: Ship it, since the new model passes 6 of 8 capability jobs where the old one passed 3
options.explanation: Capability gains do not cancel regressions. Two jobs that used to pass now fail.

options.text: Good enough, since 29 of 33 jobs passed overall, and 88% is a strong score for a new model
options.explanation: The overall number mixes both kinds of test. Regression jobs should stay near 100%.

options.text: Hold off: two regression jobs fail, and regression should stay near 100% despite gains
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says regression evals should have a nearly 100% pass rate and that a drop signals something is broken. R-07 and R-19 need a look.

options.text: Delete jobs R-07 and R-19, since the new model is clearly better at the capability jobs
options.explanation: Removing failing jobs hides the problem. A regression job is kept so that it can catch this.

questions.prompt: The wrap-around label complaint is not in the suite. What should the studio do, besides fixing this one image?

options.text: Add a wrap-around label job to the suite, so the flaw is caught again if it ever returns
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says to convert user-reported failures into test cases, and OpenAI says to grow the eval set over time.

options.text: Mention it in the team chat, since a single complaint is too small to need a test
options.explanation: A flaw that reached a client is exactly the kind of case Anthropic says to turn into a test.

options.text: Wait until three clients complain, so the flaw is clearly a pattern before testing it
options.explanation: Neither source says to wait. A real failure is a good test case on its own.

options.text: Change the rubric so upside-down logos pass, since only the client has seen one
options.explanation: Weakening the rubric hides the flaw instead of testing for it.

questions.prompt: About how often will a set of 3 images all have the logo right, using job R-12's rate?

options.text: About 90 times in 100, because each single image is right 9 times in 10
options.explanation: That is the rate for one image. All three must be right, which is lower.

options.text: About 27 times in 100, because 27 is the share of sets that fail on a logo
options.explanation: About 27 in 100 sets fail. The question asks how many are all right.

options.text: About 73 times in 100, because 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.9 equals 0.729 for three images
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's pass^k is the probability that all trials succeed. The same idea as its 0.75 x 0.75 x 0.75 example.

options.text: About 81 times in 100, because 0.9 x 0.9 equals 0.81 for each pair of images
options.explanation: That multiplies only two images. A set has three.

questions.prompt: The 25 regression jobs have scored 25 of 25 for six months. What should the studio do?

options.text: Retire the suite, since it has not found one failure in half a year of runs
options.explanation: A suite at 100% still guards against backsliding. Retiring it loses that.

options.text: Keep it, and put new hard jobs in the capability list, where there is room to grow
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says regression evals should stay near 100% to catch backsliding, and an eval at 100% gives no signal for improvement. New hard jobs belong in the capability list.

options.text: Leave it alone, since 25 of 25 proves that the model is now perfect at the job
options.explanation: A full score shows the suite is saturated. It does not prove the model is perfect.

options.text: Run it less often, since a suite at 100% is only useful once in each quarter
options.explanation: OpenAI says to run evals on every change. The pass rate does not change that.

questions.prompt: The suite lives only in the OpenAI Evals platform. What is the best plan?

options.text: Do nothing, since OpenAI will keep every eval for as long as the studio wants
options.explanation: The deprecations page gives a read-only date and a shutdown date.

options.text: Rebuild the jobs and the rubric from memory if the platform really does shut down
options.explanation: Past scores would be lost, and memory misses details. Export them while they are available.

options.text: Wait until Nov 30, 2026 to export, since that is when the platform is turned off for good
options.explanation: That is the shutdown date. Waiting for it leaves no time to copy anything.

options.text: Export the jobs, rubric and scores to files the studio owns, well before Oct 31, 2026
options.explanation: Right. The platform goes read-only on Oct 31, 2026 and is scheduled to shut down on Nov 30, 2026. Owning the files is our habit.
